scope: Supplementary tiny engine-only shared-memory cloning matrix; no Lean compiler, large memory, or full-suite claim. Original Lean tests remain unchanged.
cases: i32/i64 x (initial/maximum: 0/0, 0/2, 1/2) x workerData/postMessage/MessageChannel; at most two 64 KiB pages per case.
checks: Instantiate both transferred and freshly constructed modules using the transferred memory.
Preserve grow(0) result type and page count, valid growth, and maximum enforcement.
Preserve shared atomic writes and memory size across the worker boundary and a return transfer.
findings: Node 24.13.1 and Deno 2.9.7 pass all 18 variants. Stable Bun 1.4.2 and the measured 1.4.3-canary.1+a2b69f7b0 each pass six and fail twelve.

All six zero-capacity Bun variants crash with SIGSEGV. The pinned Bun source stores a null shared-contents handle for zero-capacity Wasm memory, but computeMemoryCost dereferences every handle. A local candidate guards this null case; a compiled fix is not yet validated.

The other six Bun failures are i64 memory/module address mismatches. The decoder hardcodes I32. The local candidate carries the address type beside the shared-contents handle, without changing serialized bytes.

The first supplemental probe called parentPort.close, absent from Deno 2.9.7. Its results are retained separately; v2 removes that redundant cleanup on all engines because the parent already terminates each worker in finally. This was a probe cleanup issue, not a Deno memory-cloning failure.
All resource counters for OOM, cap hits, throttling, and swap are zero. Child engine crashes are distinct from memory aborts.
